biography.plain_text: Jean-Philippe Chomette is a French investor who founded Algonquin, a European hotel investment and management group. An ESSEC graduate, he worked in North American finance and became a partner at Everest Capital before building the hotel business. He held a majority in its parent company when Schroders acquired the management subsidiary in 2018.

long_biography.plain_text:
Hotel investor Jean-Philippe Chomette bought established properties requiring extensive renovation, then combined refurbishment with either direct operation or management contracts. Through Algonquin's Verquin venture, he supplied capital for improvements that international hotel chains increasingly preferred other investors to finance. He targeted towns with transport connections and a balance of business and leisure guests.

Chomette also helped establish the ESSEC Foundation and its endowment. Returning to France after working abroad, he wanted his business school to have an alumni-funded capital reserve comparable to those at American universities. The fund was designed to accumulate contributions across successive generations of graduates.
